description: Full entry for a CVE, GHSA or OSV id: description, CVSS, CISA KEV status, due date, and ransomware use (kev.ransomware is true only for Known; kev.ransomwareUse is known, unknown or none), EPSS score and the date it first reached 10%, public exploits (Exploit-DB, Metasploit), affected packages with fixed versions, affected products, references and source records; where known, ATT&CK techniques (attack), ransomware groups (ransomware) and the Project Zero zero-day listing (zeroDay); vendorAdvisories holds vendor CSAF advisories and VEX statements (CISA, Red Hat): per product affected, fixed or not affected, with the remediation and a link (keep the credit of each with it); maintainerAdvisory links the advisory the maintainers published on their GitHub repository and says whether it is unreviewed (GitHub has not reviewed it yet, so the affected packages and versions are the maintainers’ word); inferredPackages (only when no record lists packages) are npm or PyPI packages inferred because a CVE product has the package’s name and the CVE references the GitHub repository the package’s registry entry names: low confidence, say "probably" and that no advisory lists them. fixes.distros gives, per Linux distro, each package’s status per release: packages are fixed (with the version; subscription, e.g. "Ubuntu Pro", "Debian ELTS" or "SUSE LTSS", when only that paid stream ships the fix, not the free archive); unfixed lines are affected with no fix, status not-fixed (no fixed version released yet) or wont-fix (the distro says it will not fix it in those releases), with builds when only that many listed builds are affected; notAffected lines are packages the distro says are not affected there. Each list is capped and more counts what was left out; keep a block’s license or credit object with its data.
